text:
jess: RFC seed - I want to propose we simplify airgapped packaging by standardizing on a single "seed+delta" bundle and pushing merge/app logic into the operator. Pros: smaller transfer, faster resume, simpler on-USB images. Cons: operator must hold more state and handle more edge cases. thoughts?
arjun: curious about rollback semantics - if operator holds state, how do we safely rollback partial applies? :thinking:
liam: agree with simplification goals. suggestion: keep content-addressed manifests and signed checkpoints so operator can verify and compute a deterministic rollback path. avoids needing a ton of bespoke operator code.
maria: counterpoint - signing+verification are heavier on operator. What about splitting verification into a lightweight sidecar/verifier process so operator remains largely control-plane and sidecar does crypto intensive work? keeps responsibilities clearer. :thumbsup:
jess: good call. tradeoff is extra binary in on-prem images. but sidecar model gives clear API boundary: operator -> verifier (gRPC) with calls: VerifyBundle(bundle_id) and StreamChunks()
liam: API sketch for verifier call: ```proto
service Verifier {
  rpc VerifyBundle(VerifyRequest) returns (VerifyResponse);
  rpc StreamChunk(StreamRequest) returns (stream ChunkStatus);
}
```
maria: +1 to proto. Also propose an "apply dry-run" mode, e.g. `operator apply --verify-only --staging` so can test without committing activation window. ops teams can run on sample nodes before broad rollout.
arjun: what about canary strategy for delta-only applies? We still need to support full-seed bootstrap in low-connectivity sites. Maybe operator should fallback to full-seed apply if delta chain incomplete. fallback must be predictable.
jess: agreed. fallback rules: 1) if delta chain verification fails -> auto-fallback to full-seed if available; 2) if full-seed unavailable -> mark node degraded and emit operator-level alert. Also expose reconciliation metrics: delta-hit-rate, verification-latency, applied-bytes.
liam: metric-driven policy is good. Also we should consider transfer resume tokens for large single-file blobs. streaming with resumable offsets reduces wasted bandwidth. simple API: StreamChunk(offset, length).
maria: security note: KMS/HSM integration for signature unwrap must be pluggable. don't bake HSM logic into operator; verifier should call KMS via plugin interface.
arjun: operator upgrade ordering: prefer apply-once-per-host with lease+quorum to avoid split-brain. operator SHOULD support a two-phase activation: Preflight -> GraceWindow -> Activate, with idempotent activation markers.
jess: long-term refactor idea: move seed creation into a 'packager' daemon that runs at build-time and publishes compact indices. operator only needs to consume indices. => smaller operator surface area.
liam: ops-bot: current full-seed sizes from CI: total image ~ 9.2GB, compressed seed tar ~ 3.8GB, typical delta ~ 120MB. streaming + resume could save hours on slow links.
ops-bot: build/seed/2024-06-24 size=3840123456 bytes delta-avg=123456789 bytes
maria: next steps: 1) draft RFC with the operator<->verifier proto + failover policy, 2) prototype verifier sidecar, 3) wire a dry-run mode into operator, 4) add metrics and a canary rollout example.
arjun: volunteers for prototype: liam + maria. I'll help design rollback tests and operator lease behavior.
jess: thanks — I'll open the RFC PR and link this thread. tagging @security for KMS review and @eng-sre for canary ops playbook.
maria: ack. I'll start a sketch of the proto and sidecar README.
liam: will pair on the prototype next week. :rocket:
